name: Thomson’s Carnot calculations
summary: Thomson set out Carnot's theory of heat engines and worked out numbers for it from Regnault's steam measurements, while weighing Joule's challenge to it.
description: On 2 January 1849 Thomson presented an account using Regnault’s steam observations, discussing Joule while provisionally retaining caloric conservation. In an appendix read 30 April 1849, he compared Regnault-derived values with Carnot’s and Clapeyron’s earlier results.
tier_reason: A bounded technical contribution, transmission episode or documented configuration useful within a specific history; no broad dependence claim is established.
why: Regnault's new steam data allowed Carnot's theory to be given numbers, while Joule's work raised doubts about its caloric basis.

links.statement: Thomson compared Clapeyron’s tabulated heat-engine values with Regnault-derived values in the appendix read 30 April 1849.
links.alternatives: Carnot’s calculations and other experimental datasets were also compared.
links.caveats: A comparison/recalculation link, not a claim that all Thomson reasoning came from one source.
links.timing: Clapeyron’s earlier table precedes the separately dated April appendix; this comparison is not assigned to the January presentation.

evidence.supports: Names Clapeyron’s table and explicitly sets its results beside Regnault-derived values.

links.statement: Thomson cited Joule’s 1843 magneto-electric paper while explaining why conserved caloric required renewed experimental scrutiny.
links.alternatives: Thomson also discussed fluid friction and sought further controls.
links.caveats: Discussion of a challenge is distinguished from complete acceptance of its interpretation.
links.timing: 1843 paper precedes the account read January 1849; this is not a response to Joule’s later June 1849 report.

evidence.locator: Collected pp. 116–117, §8 and footnote naming the 1843 paper
evidence.supports: Names the experiment and paper, frames the objection, then retains Carnot’s premise provisionally.

links.statement: Thomson made Regnault’s steam measurements the numerical basis of the account read 2 January 1849.
links.scope: Original account, p. 114 §3; the comparison with earlier tables belongs to the separate 30 April appendix.
links.alternatives: Earlier data from several fluids remained comparison points.
links.caveats: Steam-density uncertainty is not removed by this use of the tables.
links.timing: The 1847 data publication precedes the January presentation.

evidence.supports: Regnault’s steam data are the numerical basis of the original January account.
